function: Excluded, no_learning: the Quasi-NN is a model-based BFGS/backpropagation optimizer whose weights are the channel parameters, fitted per realization from pilots, with no trained model (pp. 2-3).
notes: Exclusion no_learning. p. 2: 'the Quasi-NN is fully model-based and functions as a white-box network'; p. 2: 'The parameters to be estimated are embedded in the network's weights'; p. 3: 'it differs from traditional ANNs as it is model-driven and all weights are interpretable and determinable' and 'we then use the BFGS algorithm [36] to minimize the cost function'; p. 1 abstract: 'requiring only real-time pilot signals for online network training'. The weights are the physical channel parameters (DoA, DoD, delay, gain) fitted by gradient-based optimization (backpropagation with BFGS) on each pilot observation (Algorithms 2 and 3, pp. 6 and 8); there is no offline training on a dataset and no trained parameters are reused across channels. The location-parameter database (p. 7: 'channel parameters at each RP are pre-estimated using an SU Quasi-NN and stored in an LPD') is a nearest-reference-point lookup (eq. 30), not a learned model. Borderline case for the reviewer: if the online-trained Quasi-NN were counted as learned, the area would be 2 (channel estimation, p. 1), the channel is DeepMIMO scenario O1 ray tracing (p. 9), and the baselines are only LS and OMP (p. 9), with no earlier learned method.
